title: Ancient Trees in Japan: Cities to Explore
meta_description: In Japan the old trees outlive the buildings on purpose. Shrine camphors and cedars across 81 mapped places, 205 trees, plus the country's largest.
intro: Japan is the one country on this map where the oldest trees are older than the buildings by design. Shrines are rebuilt, sometimes every twenty years as a matter of ritual, while the tree in the courtyard is left alone and wrapped in a straw rope to mark it as sacred. A camphor at a shrine gate is not decoration, it is the thing the shrine was built around. The state has protected trees as Natural Monuments since 1919, and the Environment Ministry keeps a record of every tree in the country over three metres in girth, which is why ages and measurements here are firmer than almost anywhere else in Europe. Be careful with the biggest numbers all the same: a thousand years is usually tradition rather than measurement, and the sources say so. Some places here hold one tree, which was the whole reason to travel.
